questions.stem: A voice assistant uses a text-only response model and a separate speech synthesizer. The application requires its response-text policy check to pass before any answer audio is emitted. Arrange the successful path for one recorded utterance.

options.text: Generate a text response from that transcript.
Recognize the utterance into finalized text.
Apply the required response-text policy check.
Synthesize and emit the approved response text.

explanation.whyCorrect: The text-only model needs recognition output. The policy gate consumes its answer and must precede synthesis under this application contract.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: Recognition supplies text to the response model.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: The policy check requires the candidate answer.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: The specified policy allows audio only from approved text.

questions.stem: A Custom Speech project and training data are ready. A new model must meet a held-out WER threshold before deployment, and the application will use it for real-time recognition, not batch transcription. Arrange the remaining operations.

options.text: Evaluate that model on the held-out set and confirm the WER gate passes.
Deploy the approved model to a custom endpoint.
Train the custom model with the prepared domain data.
Send real-time recognition requests to that custom endpoint.

explanation.whyCorrect: The model must exist before evaluation. The stated release gate precedes deployment, and real-time use requires a deployed custom endpoint; batch usage has a different requirement.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: Training produces the model being evaluated.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: Evaluation verifies the specified deployment gate.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Deployment creates the endpoint for this model.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Real-time requests use that deployed endpoint.

questions.stem: A Realtime assistant must interpret a recorded inspection question in the context of a written maintenance note for the same equipment. Its supported audio model and transport are ready. Host policy requires checking the returned interpretation against that note before offering a repair action. Arrange the application’s operations.

options.text: Prepare the supported audio input and text context for that equipment’s conversation.
Check that interpretation against the maintenance note before offering the repair action.
Collect the utterance and its associated maintenance note.
Submit the prepared input and obtain the successful interpretation.

explanation.whyCorrect: The audio and written context supply the model inputs. The interpretation exists after inference, and the stated host gate consumes it before an action is offered.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: The associated inputs must exist before they can be prepared.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: Input and conversation context must be prepared before submission.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: The host check consumes that interpretation and its associated note.

questions.stem: An event-based Speech SDK translator must retain the first completed translated utterance. Credentials and AudioConfig are ready. It uses a TranslationRecognizer whose recognized callback stores successful translations. Arrange initialization so the handler is ready when recognition begins.

options.text: Create the TranslationRecognizer from that translation configuration and AudioConfig.
Configure SpeechTranslationConfig with the source and target languages.
Connect the storage callback to the recognizer’s recognized event.
Start continuous recognition on the configured recognizer.

explanation.whyCorrect: The configuration is consumed by the constructor. The event belongs to the created recognizer, and this application must subscribe before starting to avoid losing its first result.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: The constructor needs the completed translation configuration.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: The recognizer must exist before its event can be subscribed.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: The application requires the callback to be ready before recognition starts.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Recognition now delivers completed results to the installed handler.

sourceRefs.title: How to recognize and translate speech

questions.stem: A store-and-forward speech translator uses manual synthesis for two target languages. It will deliver an audio file only after synthesis succeeds. Arrange the successful path for the selected target language; no translation result is available initially.

options.text: Synthesize that text with a voice supporting the selected target language.
Deliver the successfully synthesized audio file.
Select the requested language’s text from the successful result’s translations.
Recognize and translate the source utterance.

explanation.whyCorrect: The translation result supplies per-language text. Manual synthesis consumes the selected text; this file-delivery contract requires completed audio rather than a streamed partial response.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: Selection supplies the requested target text.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: Synthesis consumes that text and produces audio.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: The application delivers a file only after successful synthesis.

questions.stem: Match each workload requirement to its deployment family. Geography and model support have already been checked. Use each selected choice once; one choice is unused.

explanation.whyCorrect: Standard is usage-based interactive serving; Provisioned allocates throughput; Batch serves asynchronous work. Developer is the unused experimentation choice.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: Variable interactive demand with per-token charges: Standard.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: Allocated throughput for sustained traffic: Provisioned.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: Deferred asynchronous groups of inference requests: Batch.

questions.stem: Match each investigation to the most direct evidence source. Use each selected choice once; one choice is unused.

explanation.whyCorrect: Use operation traces for request-level timing, indexer details for ingestion failures, and service metrics for serving health. An aggregate billing report cannot localize these request, ingestion or serving failures.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: A slow operation inside one scored agent request: Correlated trace and nested spans.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Missing source documents after a partially successful run: Indexer item errors and warnings.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: Query-serving throttling during traffic peaks: Search service operational metrics.

questions.stem: Match each keyless inference observation to the boundary to inspect. Use each selected choice once; one choice is unused.

options.text: A token is acquired but the resource denies inference
The role exists only on a different resource
No Entra token can be acquired

pairs.B: Role assignment scope covering the called resource

explanation.whyCorrect: Authentication, permission and scope are separate boundaries.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: No Entra token can be acquired: Credential/authentication configuration.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: A token is acquired but the resource denies inference: Inference authorization for the caller.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: The role exists only on a different resource: Role assignment scope covering the called resource.

matchChoices: Role assignment scope covering the called resource

questions.stem: Match each trust boundary to the relevant inspection point. Use each selected choice once; one choice is unused.

options.text: An instruction inserted into a retrieved document
A harmful generated response
A user’s submitted attack instruction

explanation.whyCorrect: Protect each content boundary; a safe earlier input does not establish safety of later content.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: A user’s submitted attack instruction: User-input protection.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: An instruction inserted into a retrieved document: External-context/indirect-attack protection.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: A harmful generated response: Final-output inspection.
